_note: Original advanced concept questions for stacks.

questions.title: LIFO order
questions.code:
Stack state, bottom -> top:
A, B, C

Operation:
pop()
questions.prompt: A stack receives A, then B, then C. One item is popped. Which item comes out?
questions.explanation: A stack is last-in, first-out. C was added last, so C is popped first.

questions.title: Peek operation
questions.code:
Stack state, bottom -> top:
red, blue, green

Operation:
peek()
questions.prompt: What should `peek` do in a stack?
choices: Return the top item without removing it
questions.explanation: Peek lets you inspect the top item while leaving the stack unchanged.

questions.title: Pop trace
questions.explanation: The pop removes 5. Then 8 is pushed, so 8 is on top.

questions.title: Balanced symbols
questions.code:
Expression:
( [ ] )

Openings wait on the stack until a matching closing symbol appears.
questions.prompt: Why is a stack useful for checking balanced parentheses?
choices: The newest opening symbol must be matched first.
The oldest opening symbol must always close first.
questions.explanation: Nested symbols close in reverse order, which matches stack behavior.

questions.title: Empty pop
questions.prompt: Why should stack code check for empty before popping?
choices: Popping from an empty stack can fail or return no useful value.
questions.explanation: There is no top item in an empty stack, so the code needs a clear rule before popping.

questions.title: Reverse with a stack
questions.prompt: Arrange the steps to use a stack to reverse a list.
lines: Push each input item onto the stack.
While the stack is not empty, pop from the stack.
Append each popped item to the result.
questions.explanation: Popping returns items from newest to oldest, so the result is reversed.

questions.title: Stack ADT
questions.code:
Stack behavior:
push(item)
pop()
peek()
is_empty()
size()
questions.prompt: What does it mean to describe stack as an ADT?
choices: Describe the operations and behavior before the implementation details
Require the stack to use only arrays
Require the stack to sort values
Describe only the color of the UI
questions.explanation: An abstract data type focuses on the promised behavior, such as push, pop, peek, and is_empty. The same stack idea can be implemented with different underlying storage.

questions.title: List-backed stack
questions.code:
List-backed stack:
items = ["A", "B"]
# right side is the top
questions.prompt: If the end of a list is the stack top, which pair of operations fits best?
choices: append and pop from the end
insert at front and pop from end
questions.explanation: Adding and removing at the same end gives LIFO behavior.
